content.text: Briscola Chiamata ('Called Briscola') is the sophisticated 5-player variant of Briscolaâ€”widely considered the best form of the game. After each player receives 8 cards, an auction takes place in which the highest bidder privately 'calls' (names) a specific card. The player who holds that card becomes the Caller's secret partner for the hand, without revealing themselves. The other three form the opposing team. Card ranking and trump mechanics mirror standard Briscola.

An Italian folk development of Briscola specifically for 5 players, solving the common problem of odd player counts. The secret-partner mechanic is found in other Italian regional games (Scala Quaranta, Scopone Scientifico).

Exactly five players. With six present, one sits out each deal: that player deals to the other five and takes no part until the next hand. Deal and play are counter-clockwise; the player to dealer's right speaks first in bidding and leads to the first trick.
40-card Italian deck (A, 3, K, Q, J, 7, 6, 5, 4, 2 in 4 suits). OR: stripped French 52-card deck.
Deal 8 cards each. No trump indicatorâ€”trump is set during the auction.
